completion_conditions: Task registration injects the task's own id-scoped mirror locks, derived deterministically from the task id and goal id.
The injected set is exactly what the loop's evidence sync can write, and nothing broader — no directory glob over a shared namespace.
Frozen-plan matching accepts a registered task whose locks are the plan's locks plus exactly the derivable injected set, and rejects any other difference.
Every task in the four frozen plans passes files_outside_locks against the files the loop syncs.
Two registered tasks' injected mirror locks never conflict with each other.

decisions: The A-LOCKS narrowing was correct about product paths and wrong to drop mirror coverage with no replacement: the loop unconditionally syncs .shiki/tasks/<task>.json, .shiki/worktrees/<task>.json, .shiki/goals/<goal>.json, .shiki/locks/<task>.json and every ledger in ledger_evidence, and files_outside_locks blocks each of them.

Plan-time locks cannot name these files because the ids do not exist until registration. Injection at registration is therefore the only narrow option; a directory glob would restore the collision A-LOCKS removed.
Injected locks are id-scoped, so two tasks' injected sets are disjoint by construction and never conflict.
Frozen-plan matching must not simply ignore locks — that would let a registration widen them. It accepts plan locks plus exactly the recomputed injected set, and rejects anything else.

This goal is deliberately single-task and declares path:.shiki/** for itself. That is the circularity break: it is the one task in flight, so the blanket lock contends with nothing, and it is the task that removes the need for it.
grill_with_docs.source: Framework review 2026-07-28 (Workflow w0a858ss3), Wave 0 item 1. Verified against HEAD: 26 of 27 frozen tasks block on their own synced mirror files after the A-LOCKS narrowing, and loop_guaranteed_locks — the compensating control cited in validate_shiki's advisory docstring — does not exist.

non_goals: Exempting .shiki paths from files_outside_locks — that is ADR 0016's step B and requires the mirror-identity rule (remediation R-02) to be in force first.
Changing what the loop syncs, or the lock conflict algorithm.
Changing product-path locks declared at plan time.
outcome: A registered task's declared locks always cover the mirror files the goal loop will sync onto its branch, without any task declaring a blanket path:.shiki/** lock. Narrow product-path locks (ADR 0016 / A-LOCKS) and mirror lock coverage stop being mutually exclusive, so tasks can run concurrently and still pass files_outside_locks on their own evidence.

amendments: A1 (2026-07-29, from the independent pre-PR code review): the first implementation derived locks for the tasks/worktrees/locks/goals/dag subtrees plus one ledger path per ledger_evidence id, and omitted the paths those ledgers REFERENCE. Verified independently: a real check ledger (L-20260727T014357072057Z-4b32abe0) carries evidence ['.shiki/runner/EXEC-...json'], _evidence_relatives_for_task syncs it, and files_outside_locks flags it. The change would have passed its own PR only because this task still declares path:.shiki/** as its circularity break, while every future narrow-lock plan would break the first time a task ran its test_command. The reviewer also identified why the new tests gave false confidence — they exercise only freshly registered tasks, never a post-execution ledger. Neither the implementer nor the planner caught it; the planner's own verification hardcoded the four direct paths and never included a transitive ref.

A2 (operator-approved 2026-07-29, after a second blocking pre-PR review): the inject-at-write-time approach is structurally wrong, not merely incomplete. Round 1 found the derivation omitted transitive evidence refs; round 2 found the deeper fact — inject_mirror_locks is called at six sites in shiki_tasks.py while shiki_loop.py appends ledgers at ten sites and re-injects at none, so the TDD-gate check ledger, its runner/EXEC record and the PR ledger are synced onto the branch while the stored locks never grow to cover them. Requiring every future writer to remember to re-inject is an invariant that decays. Switch to deriving the set at judgment time, where every ledger already exists. Round 2 also found a defense-in-depth weakening — ledger_evidence is not a frozen governance field and is PR-authored in contract mode — which the derivation must bound by ownership. Both rounds passed all four of the contract's verification commands locally; the independent reviewer found all four defects anyway.

A3 (operator-approved 2026-07-29, from the CCA on PR #181): acceptance criterion 6 requires correcting the locks_cover_shiki_state advisory in scripts/validate_shiki.py, but that file was never in the task's locks, so the implementer could not touch it — MergeGate would have blocked the change as outside declared task locks. The criterion was unsatisfiable as written. This is the fifth time in this goal's lineage that the planner wrote a criterion the contract could not physically satisfy, and it is the same failure mode that induced a fabricated Spec Freeze on PR #179: when a criterion cannot be met with what the worktree grants, the cheapest path stops being honest. Lock added. The general fix — check at dispatch time that every acceptance criterion names only artifacts reachable from the task's locks and worktree — is recorded as unowned in the framework review §5.5.

A3b (operator-approved 2026-07-29): A3 added scripts/validate_shiki.py but missed the two files that pin the behaviour being corrected — tests/test_loop_lock_validator_hint.py and scripts/test_shiki_loop_lock_guard.sh, the latter asserting 'expected one .shiki/** warning for an active loop task', which criterion 6 directly contradicts. The implementer found both by refusing the repair rather than working around it, and separately proved a real gap: the repair dispatch does not sync the amended contract into the task worktree, so it read a 6-lock copy while the coordinator held 7 and correctly concluded the change was unauthorised. Locks completed; the contract is synced to the worktree before re-dispatch. Recorded for the remediation goal: a repair dispatch must carry the current contract, or the implementer judges against stale terms.
spec_freeze.source: Operator approval 2026-07-28 of Wave 0 item 1 from the framework review (Workflow w0a858ss3): restore mirror lock coverage by id-scoped injection at registration, after the A-LOCKS narrowing left 26 of 27 tasks blocking on their own synced evidence.

acceptance_checks: A registered task's locks equal its frozen plan's locks exactly — nothing is injected at registration, lock acquisition or worktree allocation.

MergeGate accepts a PR carrying the task's own mirror evidence with narrow product-path locks only, including a post-execution runner/EXEC record reached transitively through a check ledger's evidence array.
MergeGate still blocks a mirror file belonging to another task or another goal.
A task file listing a ledger that is not its own — foreign goal_id or task_id — does not expand the derived set, so a PR-authored task file cannot widen its own effective locks.
Frozen-plan matching compares locks exactly and rejects any difference, including path:.shiki/**.
validate_shiki no longer warns for a narrow-lock task on an active goal, and its advisory text no longer claims a dispatch-time .shiki lock guarantee.
non_goals: Exempting .shiki from files_outside_locks (ADR 0016 step B, needs R-02 first)
Changing the lock conflict algorithm or what the loop syncs
tasks.scope: Give a task's declared locks mirror coverage WITHOUT writing anything into the stored locks. Remove injection from every write site in scripts/shiki_tasks.py: locks stay exactly what the plan declared. Instead, scripts/mergegate_check.py derives the task's mirror set at judgment time — from its task id, goal id and its ledger_evidence, including every .shiki-prefixed path those ledgers' evidence arrays reference — and unions it into the effective lock set passed to files_outside_locks. Deriving at read time is the point: the loop appends ledgers and writes runner/EXEC records AFTER dispatch (ten append_ledger sites in shiki_loop.py, none of which re-inject), so any scheme that writes coverage into stored locks is already stale by the time MergeGate reads it. Bound the derivation so it cannot be widened by a PR-authored task file: expand only ledgers listed in the task's own ledger_evidence whose goal_id and task_id match the task, and ignore any other reference. Frozen-plan matching then compares locks exactly, with no injected-set tolerance, because nothing is injected. Finally, correct the locks_cover_shiki_state advisory in scripts/validate_shiki.py, whose message asserts a dispatch-time path:.shiki/** guarantee that no longer exists and would otherwise warn on every task registered under the new model.
tasks.test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target . && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
tasks.title: Inject id-scoped mirror locks at task registration
